[← Quantum](../index.qmd)

Study slides for the fourth course of IBM's *Understanding Quantum Information
and Computation* series, taught by John Watrous. Quantum states are fragile, so
large quantum computations need **error correction**: encoding qubits
redundantly, detecting errors without disturbing the encoded state, and
computing on encoded data without letting errors spread. The course builds
this up from the 3-bit repetition code to the threshold theorem.

**Prerequisites:** [Basics of Quantum
Information](../basics-of-quantum-information/index.qmd) and [General
Formulation of Quantum
Information](../general-formulation-of-quantum-information/index.qmd).
[Original course
page](https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/learning/en/courses/foundations-of-quantum-error-correction).

## How to study with these slides

1. Watch the lesson video, or read the original lesson.
2. Go through the deck. Press **S** for speaker notes: they hold the extra
   steps that do not fit on a slide.
3. For every code, check by hand that the stabilizer generators commute and
   work out the syndrome of each single-qubit error. That table *is* the
   decoder.

The badge exam is linked from the [original course
page](https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/learning/en/courses/foundations-of-quantum-error-correction).
